title: Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims: which cover a shipment may take
content:
## Scope

This policy of the Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims product line sets out which cover a shipment carries, which cover a cargo owner may take instead, and the product conditions a cover must meet. It applies when a cover is quoted and when it is bound.

## Policy clause

1. Every shipment carries AHL Standard Carrier Liability. The system records it and attaches it when the cargo is received, with the invoice value on file as the insured value, and it carries no premium.
2. A cargo owner may instead take AHL Declared Value Liability, by declaring the value on the transport document, or one of the CargoCare products. A CargoCare or declared value cover becomes active when it is bound at the customer's instruction.
3. The cover's cargo category must be one of the product's eligible cargo categories.
4. The insured value must be at least the product's minimum insured value and at most the product's maximum insured value of one cover.
5. The number of containers the cover takes must equal the booking's container count, unless the product allows cover of part of the booking's containers, in which case it may be lower.
6. A freight forwarder or NVOCC may hold the product only when the product allows a forwarder or NVOCC to hold it for its cargo owner. This is checked against the customer role on the customer's system record before the cover is quoted.
7. A cover is bound only for a shipment whose transport document has been drafted. This is checked against the system record of the shipment's transport document before the cover is quoted.

## Eligibility checklist

| Check | Evidence | Passes when |
|---|---|---|
| Cargo category | The cover's cargo category | It is one of the product's eligible categories |
| Insured value range | The cover's insured value | Not below the minimum and not above the maximum of one cover |
| Containers covered | The cover's container count against the booking's | Equal, or lower where the product allows part cover |
| Holder's role | Customer role on the customer record | A forwarder or NVOCC only where the product allows it |
| Transport document | Status of the shipment's transport document record | The document has been drafted |

## Hypothetical cases

- **Case A (hypothetical):** a booking carries four containers and the shipper asks for a CargoCare cover on three of them. The cover may take three containers only under a product that allows part cover; under any other product the cover must take all four.
- **Case B (hypothetical):** an NVOCC asks to hold a cover for its cargo owner. The request can proceed only under a product that allows a forwarder or NVOCC to hold it.
- **Case C (hypothetical):** a shipment's transport document has not yet been drafted. No cover is bound for that shipment until the document has been drafted.

## Points of judgement

**Is the insured value minimum inclusive?** Yes. The value must be at least the minimum and at most the maximum, so a value exactly on either figure passes.
